source.title: ImageNet Training by CPU: AlexNet in 11 Minutes and ResNet-50 in 48 Minutes
source.authors: Yang You; Zhao Zhang; Cho-Jui Hsieh; J. Demmel; K. Keutzer

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether large batches reduce held-out accuracy at a fixed epoch count, using ImageNet top-1 accuracy with LARS and warmup.
record.gate_note: The paper's own ImageNet results compare batch sizes at stated epoch counts. Prior-work results cited in the text are not recorded as rows. Table 5's learning-rate entries are excluded because they are used to tune the learning rate.
record.test_reason: The study compares ImageNet held-out accuracy across batch sizes at fixed epoch counts, testing both large-batch penalties and their recovery with LARS, warmup and normalization changes. It is not an original source for V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that LARS enables batch-32K synchronous SGD to scale across many processors while retaining baseline-like ImageNet accuracy: AlexNet in 11 minutes at 100 epochs and ResNet-50 in 20 minutes at 90 epochs. They also report 74.9% ResNet-50 accuracy in 64 epochs and 14 minutes. Their results do not establish lossless scaling at every batch size.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ImageNet top-1 accuracy to examine the large-batch training gap, with LARS and warmup as the adapted recipe; reports hardware and augmentation conditions alongside batch sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported accuracy differs with data augmentation and, in some cases, hardware and epoch count. The paper also changes AlexNet normalization to batch normalization for 32K runs.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-50 reaches 74.9% accuracy in 64 epochs and 14 minutes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A large-batch implementation can reach a specified ImageNet accuracy quickly; this result alone does not identify a fixed-epoch batch-size effect.

record.problems: The comparisons do not hold all settings constant: hardware differs across rows, and augmentation differs across conditions. Uncertainty estimates are not reported. Accuracy is used as the measure; the paper does not report training error alongside test error.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5 reports learning-rate and warmup tuning values used to select hyperparameters, which are excluded by the row rules. Cited prior-work results in Tables 3 and 4 and in the prose are not the paper's own results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and learned local connectivity.
Adam versus SGD under limited or broader tuning. LARS alone does not establish this optimizer comparison.
Language models and recovery through longer training. The 64-epoch timing result lacks a matched batch-size comparison.
Dropout effects or removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.

missing.what: Own ResNet-50 results at batch 64K: 70.0% without augmentation and 73.2% with weak augmentation, versus batch-256 baselines of 73.0% and 75.3%, all at 90 epochs.
Own no-augmentation ResNet-50 result at batch 16K: 72.7% versus the 73.0% batch-256 baseline at 90 epochs.

ResNet-50 without LARS using linear scaling and five-epoch warmup: approximately 68% at batch 16K and 56% at batch 32K, compared with a roughly 73% target and recovery with LARS. Record the matched epoch endpoint and identify the values as approximate.
missing.locator: Scaling up Batch Size; Figure 4 and caption

record.verdict_notes: V5 explicitly includes recovery through recipe adaptation, so matching small-batch accuracy supports that clause. Baseline rows cannot independently establish an effect. Table 5 is declared left out, but its test accuracies are substantive evidence of failed recovery under learning-rate/warmup tuning, not merely hyperparameter values. The text's blanket statement that augmentation is absent conflicts with later explicit augmented results; use the table-specific conditions. No uncertainty estimates establish whether the small residual differences exceed run-to-run variation.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No language models are tested. Results are for ImageNet classifiers and do not isolate batch size from all other recipe and hardware differences.
